questions.topic: eGurukul · Pulmonary Ventilation - Respiratory Muscles, Pressures
questions.stem: A patient complains of paroxysmal episodes of not being able to catch her breath. When no abnormalities are detected with conventional pulmonary function screening, the pulmonologist orders a methacholine challenge test. Which of the following will increase as a result of stimulating cholinergic receptors on the bronchial smooth muscle?
questions.solutionHtml:
Resistive work of breathing
  • Methacholine is a cholinergic agonist, which causes constriction of bronchial smooth muscle.
  • Bronchoconstriction reduces airway radius, which increases airway resistance, and thus the resistive work of breathing.


Ganong's Review of Medical Physiology, 26th Edition, Page No.649–650, 654, 657–659.

questions.topic: eGurukul · Pulmonary Ventilation - Respiratory Muscles, Pressures
questions.stem: A healthy 32-year-old woman undergoes pulmonary exercise stress testing before starting a training regimen in preparation for her first marathon. Normally, during moderate aerobic exercise, which of the following occurs?
questions.solutionHtml:
Alveolar ventilation increases
  • During moderate aerobic exercise, the body's oxygen demand increases, leading to an increase in alveolar ventilation to meet this demand. This increase in ventilation helps to increase oxygen uptake and delivery to the tissues, which is necessary for sustained exercise.


Ganong's Review of Medical Physiology, 26th Edition, Page No.74–75, 681–683.

questions.topic: eGurukul · Pulmonary Ventilation - Respiratory Muscles, Pressures
questions.stem: A patient with Wegener’s glomerulonephritis presents with sinusitis and hemoptysis. His chest radiograph shows several large cavitary pulmonary nodules, consistent with ventilation-perfusion imbalance with low V ˙ /Q˙ units. Which of the following will be greater than normal in a patient with a low V˙/Q˙ ratio?
questions.solutionHtml:
A-a gradient
  • In a patient with a low V˙/Q˙ ratio, there is a mismatch between ventilation and perfusion, leading to decreased oxygenation of the blood in the affected areas of the lungs. This results in an increased alveolar-arterial (A-a) gradient, which reflects the difference in oxygen tension between the alveoli and the arterial blood.



Ganong's Review of Medical Physiology, 26th Edition, Page No.113–116, 122–123.

questions.topic: eGurukul · Pulmonary Ventilation - Respiratory Muscles, Pressures
questions.stem: In a patterned baby with Respiratory distress syndrome, which type of cell is deficient?
questions.solutionHtml:
Type 2 alveolar cell
  • Respiratory distress syndrome (RDS) is a condition that affects premature infants and is caused by a deficiency or dysfunction of surfactant in the lungs. Surfactant is a complex mixture of lipids and proteins that are produced by type 2 alveolar cells in the lungs.


Ganong's Review of Medical Physiology, 26th Edition, Page Number: 598

questions.topic: eGurukul · Pulmonary Ventilation - Respiratory Muscles, Pressures
questions.stem: While a normal inspiration, the size of the thoracic cavity increases. According to Boyle's law true about normal inspiration is _____

options.label: A
options.text: The pressure inside the thoracic cavity decreases

options.label: B
options.text: Pressure is increased inside the thoracic cavity

questions.answerText: The pressure inside the thoracic cavity decreases
questions.solutionHtml:
The pressure inside the thoracic cavity decreases
  • According to Boyle's law, the pressure of a gas is inversely proportional to its volume. During normal inspiration, the size of the thoracic cavity increases, which results in a decrease in the pressure inside the thoracic cavity. Therefore, this is the correct statement.


Ganong's Review of Medical Physiology, 26th Edition, Page Number: 598
